summary.title: A successful Git branching model
summary.one_liner: Learn the git-flow branching model: long-lived master and develop branches plus feature, release and hotfix branches, with the Git commands for each step.
keywords: how to structure git branches for releases
fix production bug without disrupting develop
decentralized git workflow with central repo
takeaways: Use master for production-ready code (each merge to master is a tagged release) and develop as the integration branch for the next release.
Feature branches start from develop and merge back into it with --no-ff; release branches start from develop, get the version number, and merge into both master and develop.
Hotfix branches start from master for urgent production fixes and merge into both master and develop (or the current release branch).
The author notes that git-flow suits explicitly versioned software, and suggests a simpler flow such as GitHub flow for continuously delivered web apps.
summary.summary: The article, written by Vincent Driessen, presents a Git branching and release model used on several projects. It defines two long-lived branches (master for production, develop for integration) and three supporting branch types (feature, release, hotfix), each with rules about where it branches from and merges to. Each step is illustrated with concrete git commands, including version bumping, tagging, and using --no-ff merges. A 2020 reflection note at the top says the model fits versioned or multi-version software, and that continuously delivered web apps are better served by simpler workflows like GitHub flow.
